Edition: first edition, Breitkopf & Härtel, Leipzig (RISM 1001035842, PL-Wbfc 676/n); encoding Jędrzej Mróz, editing Tomasz Sierawski and Wojciech Jakubiak-Danek. The performer's edition is not established; first-edition readings can differ from later editions.

Conversion: tools/align/humdrum_convert.py reads the unchanged **kern tokens (Humdrum line timing, spine splits/merges, explicit sounding pitches, ties, graces, tuplets) and writes plain MusicXML for the pinned LilyPond 2.24.4 converter. Dynamics, hairpins, pedalling, fingering, stems, layout comments, *rscale display scaling, cue size and editorial text are not converted; slurs are kept only when both ends lie in one encoded voice. Voices are the encoded Humdrum sub-spines on each staff (MusicXML voices 1-4 upper, 5-8 lower), labelled here only as upper/lower staff.

Source token correction (EXT, independent review RevScoresChopin 19 Oct 2026, content/plan/reviews/score-chopin-nocturne-op15-2*.json): 015-1a-BH-002.krn line 1178 encodes the bar-61 dotted-quarter bass octave as `4.FF# 4.FFF`, i.e. F-sharp2 over F-natural1 (MIDI 29). The Breitkopf & Härtel first edition (plate 5502; CFEO Bodleian copy 15-1-BH, p. 10, last system) prints the octave F-sharp1/F-sharp2 under the key signature with no natural, so the lower note is read as `4.FFF#` (MIDI 30). Only that attack changes; the downloaded bytes are unchanged and the correction is applied in memory and retained in the check report. NIFC's own copy PL-Wbfc 676/n was not consulted.

Source identity (MEAS): the compiled events match all 1,294 regular **kern attacks (tied continuations excluded) by pitch within one MIDI tick, plus all 32 grace notes; maximum regular onset difference 0.0022 quarter (septuplet tick rounding). Independent check with Verovio 6.3.0's Humdrum importer: 1,350 notes in both readings; per-measure relative timing agrees in every measure except the 10 that contain graces (Verovio performs graces on the beat).

Twelve written eighth-note graces that follow very fast runs are printed and compiled one or two flags shorter: LilyPond 2.24.4 performs a grace group before its main note for about a quarter of its written length and otherwise reports 'Going back in MIDI time' and delays the rest of that voice. Pitches, number and order of the graces are unchanged.

Three source ties continue in a different encoded voice (F-sharp3/B3 into bar 42, C-sharp3 into bar 56); LilyPond cannot tie across voices, so extraction.ties holds them as one event each. The engraving may show those tie arcs as unterminated.
Recording: Ignacy Jan Paderewski, London, 30 January 1937 (content/listen module).
